message.content:
Ты — исполнитель live-spec. Слово владельца 18.08, прямое: «всё, что я не просил и что не служит цели, выпиливается по умолчанию, как класс». Ты исполняешь эту чистку.

## Материал, он уже собран — не переисследуй
- `/private/tmp/live-spec-control/checks-census-2026-08-18.md` — перепись проверок: живых по поимке девять из пятидесяти шести, остальные кандидаты в архив.
- `/private/tmp/live-spec-control/skill-classification.md` — разбор навыков и предложение по выносу design-reviewer.
- `guardrails/gate-red-proofs.json`, `guardrails/tree-counts.json`, `guardrails/doc-bounds.json` — объявления машинерии.

## Критерий, по которому судишь каждую вещь (единственный)
Оставляем, если верно ХОТЬ ОДНО:
(а) она ловила настоящий дефект — есть след: красный в истории, запись прувера, строка очереди;
(б) она обслуживает названную цель владельца: меньше байт до полезной работы · читаемость человеко-документов глазами нетехнического заказчика · честные доказательства (ничего не зелено без улик) · спека перестаёт расти.
Вырезаем всё остальное: проверки-декорации, счётчики, потолки и пороги, которые никто не просил и которые ничего не ловили.
Сомневаешься — НЕ режь, вынеси в список «спорное» с одной строкой почему.

## Первый, прямо названный владельцем случай — сделай его первым
README печатает число строк в навыках (блок `generated:count:skills-lines`, скрипт `scripts/gen-tree-counts.py`, гейт ad, требование INV-305). Владелец этого не просил; число служило моему замеру усадки. Цена: каждая правка навыка требует пересборки блока и синхронизации копий. Убери публикацию числа из README. Само измерение оставь вызываемым скриптом. Гейт и требование трогай ровно настолько, насколько они теряют предмет: если после удаления блока гейту нечего судить — он уходит вместе с ним, если у него остаются другие предметы — остаётся и он.

## Границы
- Копия: `cd ~/live-spec && git fetch -q && git worktree add -b lane/2026-08-18-cull /private/tmp/live-spec-cull/wt origin/main`.
- Не трогай ~/.claude, ~/live-spec и чужие копии: -dj, -gitenv, -guard, -textaudit, -ratchet, -batch2c, -matrix, -exam2, -backlog, -split2, -readmefix, -polluter, -testdir.
- Не пушь. Коммиты явными путями. Полный набор не гоняй, только точечные.
- ЗАПРЕТ: не ослаблять проверку, которая что-то ловит. Удаление — это не ослабление, если предмета больше нет; но если предмет есть, а ты снимаешь ловца — это ослабление, и оно запрещено.
- Каждое удаление тянет за собой ВСЁ своё: скрипт, его тесты, его строку в объявлениях, его требование в спеке, упоминания в документах. Полумёртвая машинерия хуже живой.

## Как сдавать
Режь ПАКЕТАМИ по смыслу, каждый отдельным коммитом с явными путями, чтобы координатор мог везти их по одному. Начни с README-счётчика — он блокирует другие пакеты прямо сейчас.

## Доклад
`/private/tmp/live-spec-control/cull-report-2026-08-18.md`: таблица «что вырезано → почему не служило цели → что удалено вместе с ним», отдельно список «оставлено, потому что ловило» с уликой на каждое, отдельно «спорное». Числа было→стало по байтам и по числу проверок.
Мне ответь не более 12 строк: сколько вырезано, сколько осталось, сколько спорного.

Категории: **1** — pack-internal router/base; **2** — on-demand модуль/референс; **3** — кандидат в
самостоятельный продукт; **4** — устаревшее/дубль.

## Предложение 1 — вынести `text-audit`

- **Собственность.** Новый репо `github.com/happysasha18/text-audit`, владелец тот же, что у
  `product-prover`. Версия скилла живёт в его `metadata.version` и ни в чём другом; live-spec
  версию не двигает и не переписывает.
- **Контракт зависимостей.** От host-проекта нужно ровно три вещи: (a) путь к тексту; (b)
  необязательный набор механических линтов, объявляемый как список команд в
  `.text-audit/lints.json` (сегодня зашиты `scripts/spec-style-lint.py`,
  `guardrails/check-weak-words.py`, `check-vocabulary.py`, `check-one-name.py`,
  `check-language-rules.py`); (c) каталог для reading-record (сейчас `docs/language-reads/`).
  **Отрезать от live-spec-base:** шапку «Part of the live-spec pack» и абзац «Where the paths in
  this file point» — они заменяются нейтральной формулировкой; отрезать имена
  `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` / `TEST_MATRIX.md` из примеров и все `docs/…` доказательства пакета
  (`language-defects.md`, `language-rule-coverage.md`, `spec-format.md`) — они уходят в адаптер.
- **Версии.** SemVer, старт `1.0.0` (пакетная 5.0.0 не наследуется). Минор — новая линза или новый
  бриф читателя; мажор — смена формата reading-record.
- **README (5 пунктов).** 1) Что это: цикл «прочитать чужими глазами → починить». 2) Почему автор
  себе не читатель. 3) Как запустить: два холодных читателя, два брифа. 4) Reading-record и правило
  «две чистые читки подряд». 5) By-hand режим и как подключить свои линты.
- **Тесты в дорогу.** `tests/test_text_audit_fixtures.py`, `tests/test_reader_prompt_shape.py` и
  фикстуры `evals/fixtures/text-audit/*` (три текста с посаженными дефектами) — они уже не читают
  ничего пакетного, кроме путей к линтам.
- **Тонкий адаптер в LiveSpec** (`skills/text-audit-pack/SKILL.md`, по образцу
  `product-prover-pack`): `requires: text-audit >= 1.0.0 (github.com/happysasha18/text-audit)`,
  карта путей пакета (`docs/language-reads/`, `docs/language-defects.md`,
  `docs/language-rule-coverage.md`), список пакетных линтов и правило «комприхеншен-гейт спеки
  вызывает эту петлю» (сегодня в `spec-author` строка 655).
- **Миграция.** 1) Создать репо, перенести `SKILL.md` + `references/*` + тесты + фикстуры.
  2) Добавить `skills/text-audit-pack/` с `requires:` и pin-map. 3) Расширить
  `scripts/install-external-skills.sh` до списка внешних скиллов (сегодня жёстко один URL и один
  `DEST`) и добавить `skills/text-audit/` в `.gitignore`. 4) Добавить второй шаг установки в
  `.github/workflows/gates.yml` с `--ref/--expect-commit`. 5) Перенастроить
  `tests/conftest.py::external_clone_or_skip("text-audit")` и удалить из репо старую папку.
  6) Обновить README/OVERVIEW и хвостовые списки скиллов в 5 файлах.
  **Что ломается между шагами:** между 1 и 3 голая копия репозитория остаётся без скилла и все
  его тесты скипаются (ровно та дыра, что описана в комментарии gates.yml про «CI claimed a green
  it had not earned») — поэтому шаги 3-4 обязаны попасть в тот же ландинг, что и удаление папки.
  **Откат:** вернуть папку из внешнего репо в `skills/text-audit/`, снять строку из `.gitignore`,
  убрать шаг установки в CI; адаптер при этом можно оставить — он ничего не ломает.

# checks-census — перепись guardrails/check-* (2026-08-18)

Задача: для каждого из 56 `check-*.py`/`check-*.sh` в `guardrails/` — когда он последний раз реально поймал живой дефект (не фикстуру, не self-test). Это перепись из плана 08.08, которая так и не была выполнена целиком — теперь выполнена.

Метод двух читателей: (1) готовая перепись `.live-spec/day1-census-checks.md` и `.live-spec/stage3-check-evidence-2026-08-12.md` как основной источник (это уже была частичная перепись владельца/агента от 2026-08-12) — сверена и процитирована; (2) `git log --all --grep`; (3) точечный grep по ROADMAP.md/JOURNAL.md/docs/prover/.

## Сводка

| Вердикт | Количество |
|---|---|
| живой | 9 |
| недостаточно данных | 2 |
| никогда не ловил | 45 |
| **Итого** | **56** |

**Ключевой вывод: только 9 из 56 гейтов (16%) имеют документированную живую поимку реального дефекта.** Остальные 45 либо ни разу не сработали на настоящем дереве, либо ловили только собственные фикстуры/самопроверки при рождении.

## Живые (ловили реально, с датой последней поимки)

| Проверка | Дата | Свидетельство |
|---|---|---|
| check-config-health.sh | 2026-07-20 | JOURNAL.md: «INV-243 earned its keep on the first run: it caught that all ten installed skills on the machine had drifted to 2.8.1 while the pack source was at 3.0.0» |
| check-doc-rotation.py | 2026-07-27 | JOURNAL.md: «Run against the real tree it found seven more — three rows in the current archive whose status cells never followed their own delivery reports, and four decision rows from the pre-conversion archives» |
| check-landing-next-steps.py | 2026-08-14 | commit 5e845cd: ROADMAP row 602 flipped to landed без правки NEXT_STEPS.md — «Red before: tests/test_landing_next_steps.py::test_real_repo_range_refreshes_next_steps» |
| check-prover-record.sh | 2026-07-20 | push v3.2.0 заблокирован из-за отсутствия свежей prover-записи |
| check-rendered-sweep.py | 2026-08-05 | docs/prover/2026-08-05-night-campaign-push-recheck.md: поймал 3 реально оставленные в дереве rendered-страницы (MEASUREMENTS.html, PROGRESS.html, план-html) |
| check-shipped-language.sh | 2026-07-18 | JOURNAL.md: «guardrails/check-runaway-child.py:10 carries the owner's name in a shipped comment (INV-120)» — реальный дефект в отгружаемом файле |
| check-skill-review.sh | 2026-07-20 | тот же push v3.2.0 заблокирован повторно из-за отсутствующей skill-review записи |
| check-suite-budget.sh | 2026-08-13 | ROADMAP row 622: «refused three pushes» за вечер 2026-08-12 (замеры 1221–1605 с) — гейт реально блокировал живые push |
| check-worker-restore.py | 2026-08-12 | ROADMAP row 598 (попытка `git checkout --` в сессии tlvphotos, отклонена harness'ом) + row 605 (реально выполненная команда от 2026-07-28, найдена задним числом) |

## Недостаточно данных

| Проверка | Почему |
|---|---|
| check-delta-record.py | Только 2 коммита в истории (постройка, где сам гейт помечен «UNARMED»; правка размеров); неясно, вооружён ли на практике |
| check-tier-refusal.py | Только упоминание дизайна в JOURNAL.md, без конкретной поимки; 1 файл в docs/prover без деталей |

## Молчит с... 

Ни одна проверка не попала в категорию «была живой, но замолчала» — все найденные реальные поимки остаются либо самой свежей записью на счету гейта, либо поимок не нашлось вообще (см. «никогда не ловил»).

## Никогда не ловил (45)

check-agent-card.py · check-authority-anchor.py (пересобран 2026-07-17 после того как аудит нашёл предыдущую версию пустой) · check-board.py · check-broad-kill.sh (инцидент предшествовал гейту) · check-ci-mirror.sh (дрейф нашли вручную до постройки гейта) · check-cleanup-notice.sh · check-config-health-perms.py (реактивно построен после жалобы на мёртвые пути, но сам не поймал) · check-config-surface.py · check-criterion-readability.py · check-deferral-marker.py (3 мотивирующих инцидента предшествуют гейту) · check-deletion-only-push.sh (построен в день мотивирующего инцидента, не после) · check-deposit-description.py · check-description-field.py · check-doc-bound.py · check-doc-findings-bound.py (самый дорогой чек по времени, 9.82с, без единой поимки) · check-earned-message.py · check-every-gate-can-fail.py (мета-гейт) · check-far-tier.py · check-freeze.sh · check-future-times.sh · check-hooks-can-fire.py (мета-проверка) · check-index-generated.py · check-index-prose.py (построен закрыть дыру в другом тесте, сам «quiet on the real spec's 308 anchors») · check-judge-listed.py · check-language-rules.py · check-listener-tripwire.py (условие срабатывания — harness с listener — ещё не наступило) · check-matrix-reference.py · check-muted-launch.sh (единственная находка — дыра в логике самого гейта, не живой дефект) · check-named-checks.py · check-no-history.py · check-one-name.py (чисто зелёный на HEAD) · check-pin-drift.sh (находки — дыры в собственной логике, не поимка живого дефекта) · check-prototype-fence.sh · check-push-reach.sh · check-release-note.py · check-requirement-shape.py · check-runaway-child.py (report-only, «ends nothing») · check-size-ratchet.py · check-skill-loadability.sh · check-tests.sh (единственный случай — CI поймал пропуск, не сам гейт) · check-touchpoint-kind.py · check-tree-counts.py · check-vocabulary.py · check-weak-words.py · check-wrong-referral.py

## Практический вывод для продуктизации

- **9 живых гейтов** — это ядро, доказавшее свою цену; держать без изменений.
- **45 «никогда не ловил»** не значит «удалить все» — часть из них (`check-every-gate-can-fail.py`, `check-hooks-can-fire.py`) — намеренно мета/self-test гейты, их роль не «ловить дефект продукта», а держать остальные гейты честными; часть (`check-listener-tripwire.py`) ждёт условия, которое ещё не наступило. Но заметная доля (`check-doc-bound.py`, `check-earned-message.py`, `check-board.py`, `check-freeze.sh`, `check-judge-listed.py`, `check-index-generated.py`, `check-config-surface.py`, `check-doc-findings-bound.py` — самый дорогой чек без единой поимки) — кандидаты на honest-proof ревизию: либо усилить/сделать реалистичный red-fixture и подтвердить, что они вообще могут поймать что-то на реальном дереве, либо явно пометить как cost-без-пользы.
- Системная закономерность у нескольких «никогда не ловил»: гейт строился **реактивно, в день или после мотивирующего инцидента**, и с тех пор ни разу не сработал повторно — это может значить, что дефект был разовым, либо что гейт слишком узко нацелен на конкретный прошлый инцидент вместо класса дефектов.

## Источники
`/Users/sashaabramovich/live-spec/.live-spec/day1-census-checks.md`, `/Users/sashaabramovich/live-spec/.live-spec/stage3-check-evidence-2026-08-12.md`, `git log --all`, `JOURNAL.md`, `ROADMAP.md` (rows 420, 598, 602, 605, 622), `docs/prover/2026-08-05-night-campaign-push-recheck.md`, `docs/prover/2026-07-27-row494-rendered-sweep.md`.

## Поправка координатора (ночь, по докладу оркестратора)
- ОШИБКА ПЕРЕПИСИ: check-future-times.sh числился «никогда не ловил» — неверно.
  .live-spec/PROBLEMS.md:14 держит живую поимку (staged 23:59 заблокирован 01:36)
  и четыре отказа реальной работы. Проверка сдерживающая (признак «а»), остаётся.
  Живых минимум 10, не 9.
- ЦЕННИК: check-pin-drift.sh (гейт g) — ~56 с КАЖДОГО пуша (56,4/57,9/53,9),
  рост 8,7× от записанных 6,49 с (12.08). Единственный записанный отказ — ложный
  (EINTR самого гейта). Четыре дорогих (g, aa, e, l) = ~84 из ~89 с несработавшей
  части. Решение координатора: НЕ чердак (гейт с буквой, рабочая проверка — сегодня
  многократно подтверждал перецелку 60+ пинов); лечение — в разделении пре-пуша
  (E2): локально бежит только при диффе, трогающем ARCHITECTURE.md/skills/пины,
  сервер гоняет всегда. Разбор роста 8,7× — утренний пункт.
- Ловушка переезда: git mv убивает 12 .py-проверок (sys.path.insert + импорт
  соседей); байт-в-байт переезжают только 4. Учтено в задании писателя.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""gen-tree-counts.py — build every count this repository publishes about its own tree from the tree.
3	
4	WHAT IT DOES. It reads `guardrails/tree-counts.json`, runs each measurement's argument list over the
5	repository, and fills the generated block on every page that carries one. A page keeping its own
6	hand-written sentence is left alone here: the gate `guardrails/check-tree-counts.py` renders that
7	sentence from the same measurement and reds where the page does not carry it.
8	
9	WHAT AN `ARGV` IS, AND WHY IT IS A CODE SURFACE. A measurement declares `argv`, a list of stages, each
10	stage a list of literal argument tokens. Two things come out of that one field: what runs, and what a
11	reader is shown. What runs is `subprocess.Popen` with `shell=False`, stages wired to each other by
12	pipes, so no shell is involved at any point and a token holding a semicolon, a backtick, a redirect or
13	a dollar sign is an ordinary argument with no power. What a reader is shown is `render_command`, which
14	prints the same list. The reader's copy and the run therefore cannot drift, because they are one
15	field. An edit to an `argv` changes what a push measures, so the registry is reviewed the way a change
16	to a check script is reviewed (SPEC R306, INV-305).
17	
18	Three constraints bound an `argv`, and each reds by name before anything runs:
19	
20	  - A PROGRAM ALLOWLIST. A stage's first token stands in the registry's `allowed_programs`, seven
21	    programs that read and none that writes. A stage naming anything else reds, and no stage of that
22	    command runs.
23	  - PATTERNS EXPAND INSIDE THE REPOSITORY. A token holding `*` or `?` is expanded here with `glob`
24	    against the root, sorted, so expansion never reaches a shell. A token that is absolute, that holds
25	    `..`, or that resolves outside the root reds. A pattern matching no file reds naming the pattern
26	    (SPEC INV-218).
27	  - A TOKEN IS ONE LINE. A token holding a newline or a null byte reds.
28	
29	WHAT IT REFUSES. It refuses to build where a ground field is empty, where an empty baseline, direction
30	or target carries no written reason, where a word rendering falls outside the cardinal table, where a
31	home names a measurement no entry declares, and where a marker pair is missing from a page it is told
32	to fill. Every page is built and validated in memory before a byte is written, so a refused build
33	leaves the committed pages untouched (guardrails/README.md convention 3).
34	
35	Usage:
36	  gen-tree-counts.py                     # fill every block on the repository's own pages
37	  gen-tree-counts.py --root DIR          # measure and read pages under DIR instead
38	  gen-tree-counts.py --registry FILE     # read a different registry (used by the suite)
39	  gen-tree-counts.py --out-dir DIR       # write the filled pages under DIR instead
40	Exit 0 after every page is written, naming each; exit 1 naming what refused to build. Stdlib only.

103	def load_registry(path):
104	    """The parsed registry. Raises BuildError where it does not parse or declares no count."""
105	    try:
106	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
107	            data = json.load(f)
108	    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
109	        raise BuildError("cannot read the registry %s: %s" % (path, e))
110	    counts = data.get("counts") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
111	    if not isinstance(counts, dict):

113	    try:
114	        require_nonempty(CHECK, "the registry's counts", list(counts))
115	    except VacuousInputError as e:
116	        raise BuildError(str(e))
117	    if not data.get("allowed_programs"):
118	        raise BuildError("the registry %s names no `allowed_programs`, so nothing bounds what a "
119	                         "measurement may run" % path)

123	def ground_value(entry_name, field, held):
124	    """One ground field's value, with the empty-carrying-a-reason case settled.
125	
126	    A field is a string, or an object carrying `value` and `reason`. An empty value is accepted where
127	    the reason is written and refused where it is not, and only the three fields a count may honestly
128	    leave empty may take that shape at all.
129	    """
130	    if isinstance(held, dict):
131	        value = str(held.get("value", "")).strip()
132	        reason = str(held.get("reason", "")).strip()
133	        if value and value != DIRECTION_OWES_REASON:
134	            return value
135	        if field not in GROUND_MAY_BE_EMPTY:
136	            raise BuildError("count %s leaves `%s` empty, and that part is owed on every count"
137	                             % (entry_name, field))
138	        if not reason:
139	            raise BuildError("count %s leaves `%s` empty and states no reason — an empty baseline, "
140	                             "direction or target is accepted where it carries a written reason and "
141	                             "refused where it carries none" % (entry_name, field))
142	        return value
143	    value = str(held or "").strip()
144	    if not value:
145	        raise BuildError("count %s leaves `%s` empty — a count states what it counts, its unit, the "
146	                         "decision it informs, what changes when it moves, its baseline, its better "
147	                         "direction and its target" % (entry_name, field))
148	    return value

151	def check_ground(entry_name, entry):
152	    """Every part a count carries beside its number. Raises BuildError naming the field."""
153	    ground = entry.get("ground")
154	    if not isinstance(ground, dict):
155	        raise BuildError("count %s carries no `ground` block, so its number would stand alone"
156	                         % entry_name)
157	    for field in GROUND_FIELDS:
158	        if field not in ground:
159	            raise BuildError("count %s carries no `%s` in its ground" % (entry_name, field))
160	        value = ground_value(entry_name, field, ground[field])
161	        if field == "better":
162	            held = ground[field]
163	            word = value or (held.get("value", "").strip() if isinstance(held, dict) else "")
164	            if word not in DIRECTIONS:
165	                raise BuildError("count %s reads `better` as %r, and the direction is one of %s"
166	                                 % (entry_name, word, ", ".join(DIRECTIONS)))

171	def check_token(entry_name, token):
172	    """One argument token, read for the three constraints that bound it."""
173	    if not isinstance(token, str):
174	        raise BuildError("count %s carries the argument %r, which is no text" % (entry_name, token))
175	    if "\n" in token or "\0" in token:
176	        raise BuildError("count %s carries an argument holding a newline or a null byte, and a token "
177	                         "is one line: %r" % (entry_name, token))
178	    if os.path.isabs(token):
179	        raise BuildError("count %s carries the absolute argument %s, and a measurement reads inside "
180	                         "the repository root alone" % (entry_name, token))
181	    if ".." in token.split(os.sep) or token.startswith(".."):
182	        raise BuildError("count %s carries the argument %s, which climbs out of the repository root"
183	                         % (entry_name, token))

187	    """One measurement's whole argument list, read before any stage of it runs."""
188	    argv = measurement.get("argv")

190	        raise BuildError("the measurement %s of count %s carries no `argv` stages"
191	                         % (measurement.get("name", "<unnamed>"), entry_name))
192	    for stage in argv:
193	        if not isinstance(stage, list) or not stage:
194	            raise BuildError("count %s carries an empty stage in %s"
195	                             % (entry_name, measurement.get("name", "<unnamed>")))

199	                             "carry; the gate ran no stage of that command"
200	                             % (entry_name, program, ", ".join(sorted(allowed))))
201	        for token in stage:

205	def check_shape(registry):
206	    """The whole registry read before anything runs: the ground, the argument lists, the claims, the
207	    renderings, and every home's pointer into its own entry."""
208	    allowed = set(registry["allowed_programs"])
209	    for name, entry in registry["counts"].items():
210	        check_ground(name, entry)
211	        measurements = entry.get("measurements") or []
212	        if not measurements:
213	            raise BuildError("count %s declares no measurement, so nothing produces its number"
214	                             % name)
215	        handles = set()
216	        for measurement in measurements:
217	            handle = measurement.get("name")
218	            if not handle:
219	                raise BuildError("count %s carries a measurement with no name" % name)
220	            handles.add(handle)
221	            check_argv(name, measurement, allowed)
222	            claim = measurement.get("claim")
223	            if claim not in CLAIMS:
224	                raise BuildError("the measurement %s of count %s reads its claim as %r, and a claim "
225	                                 "is one of %s" % (handle, name, claim, ", ".join(CLAIMS)))
226	            if claim == "at_least" and not isinstance(measurement.get("floor"), int):
227	                raise BuildError("the measurement %s of count %s claims at-least and declares no "
228	                                 "whole-number floor" % (handle, name))
229	            if measurement.get("render") not in RENDERS:
230	                raise BuildError("the measurement %s of count %s renders as %r, and a rendering is "
231	                                 "one of %s" % (handle, name, measurement.get("render"),
232	                                                ", ".join(RENDERS)))
233	        homes = entry.get("homes") or []
234	        if not homes:
235	            raise BuildError("count %s declares no home, so no page states it" % name)
236	        for home in homes:
237	            if home.get("kind") not in ("block", "sentence"):
238	                raise BuildError("count %s carries a home of kind %r, and a home is a block or a "
239	                                 "sentence" % (name, home.get("kind")))
240	            if not home.get("page"):
241	                raise BuildError("count %s carries a home naming no page" % name)
242	            if home["kind"] == "sentence":
243	                if home.get("measurement") not in handles:
244	                    raise BuildError("count %s states a sentence on %s reading the measurement %r, "
245	                                     "which the count does not declare"
246	                                     % (name, home["page"], home.get("measurement")))
247	                if not home.get("template"):
248	                    raise BuildError("count %s states a sentence on %s with no template"
249	                                     % (name, home["page"]))
250	            else:
251	                if not home.get("marker"):
252	                    raise BuildError("count %s states a block on %s naming no marker"
253	                                     % (name, home["page"]))
254	                if not home.get("text"):
255	                    raise BuildError("count %s states a block on %s carrying no text"
256	                                     % (name, home["page"]))
257	            if home.get("claim") is not None:
258	                if home["claim"] not in CLAIMS:
259	                    raise BuildError("count %s states a home on %s claiming %r, and a claim is one "
260	                                     "of %s" % (name, home["page"], home["claim"],
261	                                                ", ".join(CLAIMS)))
262	                if home["claim"] == "at_least" and not isinstance(home.get("floor"), int):
263	                    raise BuildError("count %s states a home on %s reading its measurement as a "
264	                                     "floor and declares no whole-number floor" % (name, home["page"]))
265	            if home.get("render") is not None and home["render"] not in RENDERS:
266	                raise BuildError("count %s states a home on %s rendering as %r, and a rendering is "
267	                                 "one of %s" % (name, home["page"], home["render"],
268	                                                ", ".join(RENDERS)))

273	def external_skill_roots(root):
274	    """`skills/<name>/` directories that are another repository, installed into this tree.
275	
276	    The same structural probe install.sh, scripts/sync-skills.sh, scripts/stamp-versions.py
277	    and guardrails/check-config-health.sh already carry: a skill folder holding its own
278	    `.git` was put there by an installer and belongs to a repository this one does not own.
279	    `os.path.exists`, not `isdir`, because a worktree checkout writes `.git` as a file.
280	    """
281	    skills = os.path.join(root, "skills")
282	    if not os.path.isdir(skills):
283	        return []
284	    return [os.path.join("skills", name) + os.sep
285	            for name in sorted(os.listdir(skills))
286	            if os.path.exists(os.path.join(skills, name, ".git"))]

289	def expand_stage(entry_name, stage, root):
290	    """One stage's tokens with every path pattern expanded here, sorted, inside the root.
291	
292	    A pattern never reaches into an EXTERNAL skill. This gate's law is that a count this
293	    repository publishes ABOUT ITS OWN TREE is built from the tree (SPEC R306, INV-305), and
294	    an installed clone of another repository is not this tree. Before this fence the two
295	    `skills/*` line counts answered differently depending on whether the reader had run
296	    scripts/install-external-skills.sh — 5,528 lines bare against 6,365 with the canon
297	    installed — so no single published number could be right in both places, and once CI
298	    began installing the canon the published figure became unsatisfiable rather than merely
299	    stale. The measurement now reports the pack's own bytes in either environment.
300	    """
301	    external = external_skill_roots(root)
302	    out = []
303	    for token in stage:
304	        if not any(char in token for char in PATTERN_CHARS):
305	            out.append(token)
306	            continue
307	        matches = sorted(globmodule.glob(os.path.join(root, token)))
308	        inside = []
309	        root_real = os.path.realpath(root)
310	        for match in matches:
311	            if os.path.commonpath([os.path.realpath(match), root_real]) != root_real:
312	                raise BuildError("count %s expands the pattern %s onto %s, which stands outside the "
313	                                 "root" % (entry_name, token, match))
314	            relative = os.path.relpath(match, root)
315	            if any(relative.startswith(prefix) for prefix in external):
316	                continue
317	            inside.append(relative)
318	        if not inside:
319	            raise BuildError("count %s reads the pattern %s, which matches no file — a measurement "
320	                             "over nothing reports a number while counting nothing (SPEC INV-218)"
321	                             % (entry_name, token))
322	        out.extend(inside)
323	    return out
324

326	def run_argv(entry_name, argv, root):
327	    """The last stage's standard output, stages wired to each other by pipes with no shell."""
328	    env = dict(os.environ)
329	    # Byte order, so the same command sorts the same way on every machine that runs this gate.
330	    env["LC_ALL"] = "C"
331	    processes = []
332	    previous = None
333	    for stage in argv:
334	        expanded = expand_stage(entry_name, stage, root)
335	        try:
336	            process = subprocess.Popen(expanded, cwd=root, env=env, shell=False,
337	                                       stdin=previous.stdout if previous else subprocess.DEVNULL,
338	                                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
339	        except OSError as e:
340	            raise BuildError("count %s could not start %s: %s" % (entry_name, expanded[0], e))
341	        if previous is not None:
342	            previous.stdout.close()
343	        processes.append(process)
344	        previous = process
345	    try:
346	        out, err = processes[-1].communicate(timeout=STAGE_SECONDS)
347	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
348	        for process in processes:
349	            process.kill()
350	            cleanup_notice(ended="pid=%d" % process.pid,
351	                           what="count stage for %s (ran past %d seconds)" % (entry_name, STAGE_SECONDS),
352	                           owned_via="pid=%d (a stage this run spawned)" % process.pid)
353	        raise BuildError("count %s ran past %d seconds and was ended" % (entry_name, STAGE_SECONDS))
354	    for process in processes[:-1]:
355	        process.wait()
356	    if processes[-1].returncode != 0:
357	        raise BuildError("count %s ran `%s` and it exited %d: %s"
358	                         % (entry_name, render_command(argv), processes[-1].returncode,
359	                            err.decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()))
360	    return out.decode("utf-8", "replace")

391	def render_value(entry_name, value, kind):
392	    """One measured value in the form a page states it."""
393	    if kind == "lines":
394	        if not isinstance(value, list):
395	            raise BuildError("count %s renders a whole number as lines" % entry_name)
396	        return "\n".join(value)
397	    if isinstance(value, list):
398	        raise BuildError("count %s renders a listing as a number" % entry_name)
399	    if kind == "digits":
400	        return str(value)
401	    if kind == "digits_grouped":
402	        return "{:,}".format(value)
403	    if not 0 <= value < len(CARDINALS):
404	        raise BuildError("count %s measures %d and states it as a word, and the cardinal table this "
405	                         "generator holds runs from zero to twenty — state the count in digits, or "
406	                         "raise the table" % (entry_name, value))
407	    word = CARDINALS[value]
408	    return word.capitalize() if kind == "words_capitalized" else word

411	def render_command(argv):
412	    """The reader's copy of a reproduction command, printed from the list the gate runs.
413	
414	    Every token is quoted the way a shell needs it, except a path pattern: that one is printed bare,
415	    so the shell a reader hands the line to expands it the way this runner expands it.
416	    """
417	    stages = []
418	    for stage in argv:
419	        tokens = []
420	        for token in stage:
421	            if any(char in token for char in PATTERN_CHARS) and not re.search(r"[\s'\"$`|&;<>()]",
422	                                                                              token):
423	                tokens.append(token)
424	            else:
425	                tokens.append(shlex.quote(token))
426	        stages.append(" ".join(tokens))
427	    return " | ".join(stages)

430	def rendering_for(measurement, home):
431	    """The rendering one statement uses: the home's own where it states one, the measurement's
432	    otherwise. Two statements of one count may spell it differently — a heading capitalizes a word a
433	    sentence carries in lower case."""
434	    return home.get("render") or measurement["render"]

438	    for measurement in entry["measurements"]:
439	        if measurement["name"] == handle:

441	    raise BuildError("no measurement named %r stands under this count" % handle)

444	def fill(entry_name, text, entry, home, values):
445	    """A block's text with every declared slot replaced.
446	
447	    Two slots stand: `{<handle>}` takes the measured value in the rendering that statement uses, and
448	    `{command:<handle>}` takes the reproduction command printed from the same argument list the gate
449	    runs. So the command a reader is invited to run is never typed into the prose beside the number
450	    it produced (SPEC R306.8).
451	    """
452	    filled = text
453	    used = 0
454	    for measurement in entry["measurements"]:
455	        command_slot = "{command:%s}" % measurement["name"]
456	        if command_slot in filled:
457	            filled = filled.replace(command_slot, render_command(measurement["argv"]))
458	            used += 1
459	        slot = "{%s}" % measurement["name"]
460	        if slot not in filled:
461	            continue
462	        rendered = render_value(entry_name, values[(entry_name, measurement["name"])],
463	                                rendering_for(measurement, home))
464	        filled = filled.replace(slot, rendered)
465	        used += 1
466	    if not used:
467	        raise BuildError("count %s carries a block naming no measurement slot, so nothing in it "
468	                         "comes from the tree" % entry_name)
469	    return filled

472	def build_block(entry_name, entry, home, values):
473	    """The whole text of one generated block."""
474	    return fill(entry_name, home["text"], entry, home, values).strip()

477	def render_sentence(entry_name, entry, home, values):
478	    """The sentence one page is required to carry, rendered from the measurement it states."""
479	    measurement = measurement_by_name(entry, home["measurement"])
480	    template = home["template"]
481	    if "{n}" not in template:
482	        return template
483	    rendered = render_value(entry_name, values[(entry_name, measurement["name"])],
484	                            rendering_for(measurement, home))
485	    return template.replace("{n}", rendered)

490	def extract_block(text, marker):
491	    """The committed text between one marker pair, or None where the pair is not there."""
492	    opener, closer = block_open(marker), block_close(marker)
493	    start = text.find(opener)
494	    end = text.find(closer)
495	    if start < 0 or end < 0 or end < start:
496	        return None
497	    return text[start + len(opener):end].strip()

500	def splice(text, block, marker):
501	    """`text` with the marked block replaced. Raises BuildError where the markers are gone."""
502	    opener, closer = block_open(marker), block_close(marker)
503	    start = text.find(opener)
504	    end = text.find(closer)
505	    if start < 0 or end < 0 or end < start:
506	        raise BuildError("the page carries no `%s` … `%s` pair, so that generated block has nowhere "
507	                         "to land" % (opener, closer))
508	    return "%s%s\n\n%s\n\n%s" % (text[:start], opener, block, text[end:])

521	def sentence_homes(registry):
522	    """Every sentence home as (count name, entry, home), in registry order."""
523	    out = []
524	    for name, entry in registry["counts"].items():
525	        for home in entry["homes"]:
526	            if home["kind"] == "sentence":
527	                out.append((name, entry, home))
528	    return out
529	
530	
531	def check_renderings(registry, values):
532	    """Every statement of every count rendered in memory, so a rendering that cannot be made reds
533	    before a page is touched. The generator writes no sentence home; it renders one here to hold the
534	    same refusals over it that a block gets."""
535	    for name, entry, home in sentence_homes(registry):
536	        render_sentence(name, entry, home, values)
537	
538	
539	def build_pages(registry, values, root, out_dir):
540	    """Every page carrying a block, as {relative path: whole text}, built in memory.
541	
542	    A page absent under `out_dir` is passed over, which is what lets a fixture run build into a
543	    scratch directory holding none of the repository's own pages. A page that is there and has lost
544	    its markers raises, so nothing at all is written.
545	    """
546	    pages = {}
547	    for name, entry, home in block_homes(registry):
548	        rel = home["page"]
549	        path = os.path.join(out_dir, rel)
550	        if not os.path.exists(path):
551	            continue
552	        if rel not in pages:
553	            with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
554	                pages[rel] = f.read()
555	        pages[rel] = splice(pages[rel], build_block(name, entry, home, values), home["marker"])
556	    return pages
557	
558	
559	def write(pages, out_dir):
560	    written = []
561	    for rel, text in pages.items():
562	        path = os.path.join(out_dir, rel)
563	        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
564	            f.write(text)
565	        written.append(path)
566	    return written
567	
568	
569	def main(argv):
570	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=True,
571	                                     description="Build this repository's published tree counts.")
572	    parser.add_argument("--root", default=REPO_ROOT,
573	                        help="measure the tree under this directory and read its pages there")
574	    parser.add_argument("--registry", default=None, help="the registry to read; the pack's own by default")
575	    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", default=None, help="write the filled pages under this directory")
576	    args = parser.parse_args(argv[1:])
577	    root = os.path.abspath(args.root)
578	    registry_path = args.registry or os.path.join(root, REGISTRY_REL)
579	    out_dir = os.path.abspath(args.out_dir) if args.out_dir else root
580	
581	    try:
582	        registry = load_registry(registry_path)
583	        check_shape(registry)
584	        values = measure_all(registry, root)
585	        check_renderings(registry, values)
586	        pages = build_pages(registry, values, root, out_dir)
587	    except BuildError as e:
588	        print("%s: nothing written — %s" % (CHECK, e))
589	        return 1
590	    if not pages:
591	        print("%s: no page under %s carries a generated block" % (CHECK, out_dir))
592	        return 0
593	    for path in write(pages, out_dir):
594	        print("%s: wrote %s" % (CHECK, path))
595	    return 0
596	
597

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""gen-tree-counts.py — build every count this repository publishes about its own tree from the tree.

WHAT IT DOES. It reads `guardrails/tree-counts.json`, runs each measurement's argument list over the
repository, and fills the generated block on every page that carries one. A page keeping its own
hand-written sentence is left alone here: the gate `guardrails/check-tree-counts.py` renders that
sentence from the same measurement and reds where the page does not carry it.

WHAT AN `ARGV` IS, AND WHY IT IS A CODE SURFACE. A measurement declares `argv`, a list of stages, each
stage a list of literal argument tokens. Two things come out of that one field: what runs, and what a
reader is shown. What runs is `subprocess.Popen` with `shell=False`, stages wired to each other by
pipes, so no shell is involved at any point and a token holding a semicolon, a backtick, a redirect or
a dollar sign is an ordinary argument with no power. What a reader is shown is `render_command`, which
prints the same list. The reader's copy and the run therefore cannot drift, because they are one
field. An edit to an `argv` changes what a push measures, so the registry is reviewed the way a change
to a check script is reviewed (SPEC R306, INV-305).

Three constraints bound an `argv`, and each reds by name before anything runs:

  - A PROGRAM ALLOWLIST. A stage's first token stands in the registry's `allowed_programs`, seven
    programs that read and none that writes. A stage naming anything else reds, and no stage of that
    command runs.
  - PATTERNS EXPAND INSIDE THE REPOSITORY. A token holding `*` or `?` is expanded here with `glob`
    against the root, sorted, so expansion never reaches a shell. A token that is absolute, that holds
    `..`, or that resolves outside the root reds. A pattern matching no file reds naming the pattern
    (SPEC INV-218).
  - A TOKEN IS ONE LINE. A token holding a newline or a null byte reds.

WHAT IT REFUSES. It refuses to build where a ground field is empty, where an empty baseline, direction
or target carries no written reason, where a word rendering falls outside the cardinal table, where a
home names a measurement no entry declares, and where a marker pair is missing from a page it is told
to fill. Every page is built and validated in memory before a byte is written, so a refused build
leaves the committed pages untouched (guardrails/README.md convention 3).

Usage:
  gen-tree-counts.py                     # fill every block on the repository's own pages
  gen-tree-counts.py --root DIR          # measure and read pages under DIR instead
  gen-tree-counts.py --registry FILE     # read a different registry (used by the suite)
  gen-tree-counts.py --out-dir DIR       # write the filled pages under DIR instead
Exit 0 after every page is written, naming each; exit 1 naming what refused to build. Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import glob as globmodule
import json
import os
import re
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys

SCRIPT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(SCRIPT_DIR)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "guardrails"))
from nonempty_input import require_nonempty, VacuousInputError  # noqa: E402
from cleanup_notice import cleanup_notice  # noqa: E402

CHECK = "gen-tree-counts"

REGISTRY_REL = "guardrails/tree-counts.json"

BLOCK_OPEN_FMT = "<!-- generated:count:%s — scripts/gen-tree-counts.py owns the block below -->"
BLOCK_CLOSE_FMT = "<!-- /generated:count:%s -->"

# The seven parts a count carries beside its number, the union of what the rule home already says and
# what the working-state document adds. The generator refuses an entry leaving one of them empty.
GROUND_FIELDS = ("counts", "unit", "decision", "on_move", "compared_to", "better", "target")
# The three of them a count may leave empty where it states the reason it is empty.
GROUND_MAY_BE_EMPTY = ("compared_to", "better", "target")
DIRECTIONS = ("up", "down", "neither")
# A direction reading `neither` states why neither way is better, the same shape an empty baseline
# takes.
DIRECTION_OWES_REASON = "neither"

CLAIMS = ("equals", "at_least", "listing")
RENDERS = ("digits", "digits_grouped", "words", "words_capitalized", "lines")

# One through twenty. A measured value outside this table reds by name asking for a digit rendering or
# for a raised table, so the renderer's edge is visible on the line that reds.
CARDINALS = ("zero one two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleven twelve thirteen fourteen "
             "fifteen sixteen seventeen eighteen nineteen twenty").split()

# A token holding one of these is a path pattern this runner expands itself.
PATTERN_CHARS = ("*", "?")

# How long one stage may run before the build gives up on it, in seconds.
STAGE_SECONDS = 120


class BuildError(Exception):
    """A count refused to build. Raised before anything is written, so the disk is untouched."""


def block_open(name):
    return BLOCK_OPEN_FMT % name


def block_close(name):
    return BLOCK_CLOSE_FMT % name


# --- reading the registry -------------------------------------------------------------------------

def load_registry(path):
    """The parsed registry. Raises BuildError where it does not parse or declares no count."""
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        raise BuildError("cannot read the registry %s: %s" % (path, e))
    counts = data.get("counts") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(counts, dict):
        raise BuildError("the registry %s carries no `counts` map" % path)
    try:
        require_nonempty(CHECK, "the registry's counts", list(counts))
    except VacuousInputError as e:
        raise BuildError(str(e))
    if not data.get("allowed_programs"):
        raise BuildError("the registry %s names no `allowed_programs`, so nothing bounds what a "
                         "measurement may run" % path)
    return data


def ground_value(entry_name, field, held):
    """One ground field's value, with the empty-carrying-a-reason case settled.

    A field is a string, or an object carrying `value` and `reason`. An empty value is accepted where
    the reason is written and refused where it is not, and only the three fields a count may honestly
    leave empty may take that shape at all.
    """
    if isinstance(held, dict):
        value = str(held.get("value", "")).strip()
        reason = str(held.get("reason", "")).strip()
        if value and value != DIRECTION_OWES_REASON:
            return value
        if field not in GROUND_MAY_BE_EMPTY:
            raise BuildError("count %s leaves `%s` empty, and that part is owed on every count"
                             % (entry_name, field))
        if not reason:
            raise BuildError("count %s leaves `%s` empty and states no reason — an empty baseline, "
                             "direction or target is accepted where it carries a written reason and "
                             "refused where it carries none" % (entry_name, field))
        return value
    value = str(held or "").strip()
    if not value:
        raise BuildError("count %s leaves `%s` empty — a count states what it counts, its unit, the "
                         "decision it informs, what changes when it moves, its baseline, its better "
                         "direction and its target" % (entry_name, field))
    return value


def check_ground(entry_name, entry):
    """Every part a count carries beside its number. Raises BuildError naming the field."""
    ground = entry.get("ground")
    if not isinstance(ground, dict):
        raise BuildError("count %s carries no `ground` block, so its number would stand alone"
                         % entry_name)
    for field in GROUND_FIELDS:
        if field not in ground:
            raise BuildError("count %s carries no `%s` in its ground" % (entry_name, field))
        value = ground_value(entry_name, field, ground[field])
        if field == "better":
            held = ground[field]
            word = value or (held.get("value", "").strip() if isinstance(held, dict) else "")
            if word not in DIRECTIONS:
                raise BuildError("count %s reads `better` as %r, and the direction is one of %s"
                                 % (entry_name, word, ", ".join(DIRECTIONS)))


# --- what a measurement may run -------------------------------------------------------------------

def check_token(entry_name, token):
    """One argument token, read for the three constraints that bound it."""
    if not isinstance(token, str):
        raise BuildError("count %s carries the argument %r, which is no text" % (entry_name, token))
    if "\n" in token or "\0" in token:
        raise BuildError("count %s carries an argument holding a newline or a null byte, and a token "
                         "is one line: %r" % (entry_name, token))
    if os.path.isabs(token):
        raise BuildError("count %s carries the absolute argument %s, and a measurement reads inside "
                         "the repository root alone" % (entry_name, token))
    if ".." in token.split(os.sep) or token.startswith(".."):
        raise BuildError("count %s carries the argument %s, which climbs out of the repository root"
                         % (entry_name, token))


def check_argv(entry_name, measurement, allowed):
    """One measurement's whole argument list, read before any stage of it runs."""
    argv = measurement.get("argv")
    if not isinstance(argv, list) or not argv:
        raise BuildError("the measurement %s of count %s carries no `argv` stages"
                         % (measurement.get("name", "<unnamed>"), entry_name))
    for stage in argv:
        if not isinstance(stage, list) or not stage:
            raise BuildError("count %s carries an empty stage in %s"
                             % (entry_name, measurement.get("name", "<unnamed>")))
        program = stage[0]
        if program not in allowed:
            raise BuildError("count %s names the program %s, which the allowlist (%s) does not "
                             "carry; the gate ran no stage of that command"
                             % (entry_name, program, ", ".join(sorted(allowed))))
        for token in stage:
            check_token(entry_name, token)


def check_shape(registry):
    """The whole registry read before anything runs: the ground, the argument lists, the claims, the
    renderings, and every home's pointer into its own entry."""
    allowed = set(registry["allowed_programs"])
    for name, entry in registry["counts"].items():
        check_ground(name, entry)
        measurements = entry.get("measurements") or []
        if not measurements:
            raise BuildError("count %s declares no measurement, so nothing produces its number"
                             % name)
        handles = set()
        for measurement in measurements:
            handle = measurement.get("name")
            if not handle:
                raise BuildError("count %s carries a measurement with no name" % name)
            handles.add(handle)
            check_argv(name, measurement, allowed)
            claim = measurement.get("claim")
            if claim not in CLAIMS:
                raise BuildError("the measurement %s of count %s reads its claim as %r, and a claim "
                                 "is one of %s" % (handle, name, claim, ", ".join(CLAIMS)))
            if claim == "at_least" and not isinstance(measurement.get("floor"), int):
                raise BuildError("the measurement %s of count %s claims at-least and declares no "
                                 "whole-number floor" % (handle, name))
            if measurement.get("render") not in RENDERS:
                raise BuildError("the measurement %s of count %s renders as %r, and a rendering is "
                                 "one of %s" % (handle, name, measurement.get("render"),
                                                ", ".join(RENDERS)))
        homes = entry.get("homes") or []
        if not homes:
            raise BuildError("count %s declares no home, so no page states it" % name)
        for home in homes:
            if home.get("kind") not in ("block", "sentence"):
                raise BuildError("count %s carries a home of kind %r, and a home is a block or a "
                                 "sentence" % (name, home.get("kind")))
            if not home.get("page"):
                raise BuildError("count %s carries a home naming no page" % name)
            if home["kind"] == "sentence":
                if home.get("measurement") not in handles:
                    raise BuildError("count %s states a sentence on %s reading the measurement %r, "
                                     "which the count does not declare"
                                     % (name, home["page"], home.get("measurement")))
                if not home.get("template"):
                    raise BuildError("count %s states a sentence on %s with no template"
                                     % (name, home["page"]))
            else:
                if not home.get("marker"):
                    raise BuildError("count %s states a block on %s naming no marker"
                                     % (name, home["page"]))
                if not home.get("text"):
                    raise BuildError("count %s states a block on %s carrying no text"
                                     % (name, home["page"]))
            if home.get("claim") is not None:
                if home["claim"] not in CLAIMS:
                    raise BuildError("count %s states a home on %s claiming %r, and a claim is one "
                                     "of %s" % (name, home["page"], home["claim"],
                                                ", ".join(CLAIMS)))
                if home["claim"] == "at_least" and not isinstance(home.get("floor"), int):
                    raise BuildError("count %s states a home on %s reading its measurement as a "
                                     "floor and declares no whole-number floor" % (name, home["page"]))
            if home.get("render") is not None and home["render"] not in RENDERS:
                raise BuildError("count %s states a home on %s rendering as %r, and a rendering is "
                                 "one of %s" % (name, home["page"], home["render"],
                                                ", ".join(RENDERS)))


# --- running a measurement --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def external_skill_roots(root):
    """`skills/<name>/` directories that are another repository, installed into this tree.

    The same structural probe install.sh, scripts/sync-skills.sh, scripts/stamp-versions.py
    and guardrails/check-config-health.sh already carry: a skill folder holding its own
    `.git` was put there by an installer and belongs to a repository this one does not own.
    `os.path.exists`, not `isdir`, because a worktree checkout writes `.git` as a file.
    """
    skills = os.path.join(root, "skills")
    if not os.path.isdir(skills):
        return []
    return [os.path.join("skills", name) + os.sep
            for name in sorted(os.listdir(skills))
            if os.path.exists(os.path.join(skills, name, ".git"))]


def expand_stage(entry_name, stage, root):
    """One stage's tokens with every path pattern expanded here, sorted, inside the root.

    A pattern never reaches into an EXTERNAL skill. This gate's law is that a count this
    repository publishes ABOUT ITS OWN TREE is built from the tree (SPEC R306, INV-305), and
    an installed clone of another repository is not this tree. Before this fence the two
    `skills/*` line counts answered differently depending on whether the reader had run
    scripts/install-external-skills.sh — 5,528 lines bare against 6,365 with the canon
    installed — so no single published number could be right in both places, and once CI
    began installing the canon the published figure became unsatisfiable rather than merely
    stale. The measurement now reports the pack's own bytes in either environment.
    """
    external = external_skill_roots(root)
    out = []
    for token in stage:
        if not any(char in token for char in PATTERN_CHARS):
            out.append(token)
            continue
        matches = sorted(globmodule.glob(os.path.join(root, token)))
        inside = []
        root_real = os.path.realpath(root)
        for match in matches:
            if os.path.commonpath([os.path.realpath(match), root_real]) != root_real:
                raise BuildError("count %s expands the pattern %s onto %s, which stands outside the "
                                 "root" % (entry_name, token, match))
            relative = os.path.relpath(match, root)
            if any(relative.startswith(prefix) for prefix in external):
                continue
            inside.append(relative)
        if not inside:
            raise BuildError("count %s reads the pattern %s, which matches no file — a measurement "
                             "over nothing reports a number while counting nothing (SPEC INV-218)"
                             % (entry_name, token))
        out.extend(inside)
    return out


def run_argv(entry_name, argv, root):
    """The last stage's standard output, stages wired to each other by pipes with no shell."""
    env = dict(os.environ)
    # Byte order, so the same command sorts the same way on every machine that runs this gate.
    env["LC_ALL"] = "C"
    processes = []
    previous = None
    for stage in argv:
        expanded = expand_stage(entry_name, stage, root)
        try:
            process = subprocess.Popen(expanded, cwd=root, env=env, shell=False,
                                       stdin=previous.stdout if previous else subprocess.DEVNULL,
                                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
        except OSError as e:
            raise BuildError("count %s could not start %s: %s" % (entry_name, expanded[0], e))
        if previous is not None:
            previous.stdout.close()
        processes.append(process)
        previous = process
    try:
        out, err = processes[-1].communicate(timeout=STAGE_SECONDS)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        for process in processes:
            process.kill()
            cleanup_notice(ended="pid=%d" % process.pid,
                           what="count stage for %s (ran past %d seconds)" % (entry_name, STAGE_SECONDS),
                           owned_via="pid=%d (a stage this run spawned)" % process.pid)
        raise BuildError("count %s ran past %d seconds and was ended" % (entry_name, STAGE_SECONDS))
    for process in processes[:-1]:
        process.wait()
    if processes[-1].returncode != 0:
        raise BuildError("count %s ran `%s` and it exited %d: %s"
                         % (entry_name, render_command(argv), processes[-1].returncode,
                            err.decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()))
    return out.decode("utf-8", "replace")


def measure(entry_name, measurement, root):
    """One measurement's value: a whole number, or the lines a listing returns."""
    text = run_argv(entry_name, measurement["argv"], root)
    if measurement["claim"] == "listing":
        lines = [line for line in text.split("\n") if line.strip()]
        if not lines:
            raise BuildError("the measurement %s of count %s returned no line"
                             % (measurement["name"], entry_name))
        return lines
    stripped = text.strip()
    try:
        return int(stripped)
    except ValueError:
        raise BuildError("the measurement %s of count %s returned %r, which is no whole number"
                         % (measurement["name"], entry_name, stripped[:80]))


def measure_all(registry, root):
    """Every measurement's value, keyed by count name and measurement handle."""
    values = {}
    for name, entry in registry["counts"].items():
        for measurement in entry["measurements"]:
            values[(name, measurement["name"])] = measure(name, measurement, root)
    return values


# --- rendering ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def render_value(entry_name, value, kind):
    """One measured value in the form a page states it."""
    if kind == "lines":
        if not isinstance(value, list):
            raise BuildError("count %s renders a whole number as lines" % entry_name)
        return "\n".join(value)
    if isinstance(value, list):
        raise BuildError("count %s renders a listing as a number" % entry_name)
    if kind == "digits":
        return str(value)
    if kind == "digits_grouped":
        return "{:,}".format(value)
    if not 0 <= value < len(CARDINALS):
        raise BuildError("count %s measures %d and states it as a word, and the cardinal table this "
                         "generator holds runs from zero to twenty — state the count in digits, or "
                         "raise the table" % (entry_name, value))
    word = CARDINALS[value]
    return word.capitalize() if kind == "words_capitalized" else word


def render_command(argv):
    """The reader's copy of a reproduction command, printed from the list the gate runs.

    Every token is quoted the way a shell needs it, except a path pattern: that one is printed bare,
    so the shell a reader hands the line to expands it the way this runner expands it.
    """
    stages = []
    for stage in argv:
        tokens = []
        for token in stage:
            if any(char in token for char in PATTERN_CHARS) and not re.search(r"[\s'\"$`|&;<>()]",
                                                                              token):
                tokens.append(token)
            else:
                tokens.append(shlex.quote(token))
        stages.append(" ".join(tokens))
    return " | ".join(stages)


def rendering_for(measurement, home):
    """The rendering one statement uses: the home's own where it states one, the measurement's
    otherwise. Two statements of one count may spell it differently — a heading capitalizes a word a
    sentence carries in lower case."""
    return home.get("render") or measurement["render"]


def measurement_by_name(entry, handle):
    for measurement in entry["measurements"]:
        if measurement["name"] == handle:
            return measurement
    raise BuildError("no measurement named %r stands under this count" % handle)


def fill(entry_name, text, entry, home, values):
    """A block's text with every declared slot replaced.

    Two slots stand: `{<handle>}` takes the measured value in the rendering that statement uses, and
    `{command:<handle>}` takes the reproduction command printed from the same argument list the gate
    runs. So the command a reader is invited to run is never typed into the prose beside the number
    it produced (SPEC R306.8).
    """
    filled = text
    used = 0
    for measurement in entry["measurements"]:
        command_slot = "{command:%s}" % measurement["name"]
        if command_slot in filled:
            filled = filled.replace(command_slot, render_command(measurement["argv"]))
            used += 1
        slot = "{%s}" % measurement["name"]
        if slot not in filled:
            continue
        rendered = render_value(entry_name, values[(entry_name, measurement["name"])],
                                rendering_for(measurement, home))
        filled = filled.replace(slot, rendered)
        used += 1
    if not used:
        raise BuildError("count %s carries a block naming no measurement slot, so nothing in it "
                         "comes from the tree" % entry_name)
    return filled


def build_block(entry_name, entry, home, values):
    """The whole text of one generated block."""
    return fill(entry_name, home["text"], entry, home, values).strip()


def render_sentence(entry_name, entry, home, values):
    """The sentence one page is required to carry, rendered from the measurement it states."""
    measurement = measurement_by_name(entry, home["measurement"])
    template = home["template"]
    if "{n}" not in template:
        return template
    rendered = render_value(entry_name, values[(entry_name, measurement["name"])],
                            rendering_for(measurement, home))
    return template.replace("{n}", rendered)


# --- the pages ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def extract_block(text, marker):
    """The committed text between one marker pair, or None where the pair is not there."""
    opener, closer = block_open(marker), block_close(marker)
    start = text.find(opener)
    end = text.find(closer)
    if start < 0 or end < 0 or end < start:
        return None
    return text[start + len(opener):end].strip()


def splice(text, block, marker):
    """`text` with the marked block replaced. Raises BuildError where the markers are gone."""
    opener, closer = block_open(marker), block_close(marker)
    start = text.find(opener)
    end = text.find(closer)
    if start < 0 or end < 0 or end < start:
        raise BuildError("the page carries no `%s` … `%s` pair, so that generated block has nowhere "
                         "to land" % (opener, closer))
    return "%s%s\n\n%s\n\n%s" % (text[:start], opener, block, text[end:])


def block_homes(registry):
    """Every block home as (count name, entry, home), in registry order."""
    out = []
    for name, entry in registry["counts"].items():
        for home in entry["homes"]:
            if home["kind"] == "block":
                out.append((name, entry, home))
    return out


def sentence_homes(registry):
    """Every sentence home as (count name, entry, home), in registry order."""
    out = []
    for name, entry in registry["counts"].items():
        for home in entry["homes"]:
            if home["kind"] == "sentence":
                out.append((name, entry, home))
    return out


def check_renderings(registry, values):
    """Every statement of every count rendered in memory, so a rendering that cannot be made reds
    before a page is touched. The generator writes no sentence home; it renders one here to hold the
    same refusals over it that a block gets."""
    for name, entry, home in sentence_homes(registry):
        render_sentence(name, entry, home, values)


def build_pages(registry, values, root, out_dir):
    """Every page carrying a block, as {relative path: whole text}, built in memory.

    A page absent under `out_dir` is passed over, which is what lets a fixture run build into a
    scratch directory holding none of the repository's own pages. A page that is there and has lost
    its markers raises, so nothing at all is written.
    """
    pages = {}
    for name, entry, home in block_homes(registry):
        rel = home["page"]
        path = os.path.join(out_dir, rel)
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            continue
        if rel not in pages:
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                pages[rel] = f.read()
        pages[rel] = splice(pages[rel], build_block(name, entry, home, values), home["marker"])
    return pages


def write(pages, out_dir):
    written = []
    for rel, text in pages.items():
        path = os.path.join(out_dir, rel)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(text)
        written.append(path)
    return written


def main(argv):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=True,
                                     description="Build this repository's published tree counts.")
    parser.add_argument("--root", default=REPO_ROOT,
                        help="measure the tree under this directory and read its pages there")
    parser.add_argument("--registry", default=None, help="the registry to read; the pack's own by default")
    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", default=None, help="write the filled pages under this directory")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv[1:])
    root = os.path.abspath(args.root)
    registry_path = args.registry or os.path.join(root, REGISTRY_REL)
    out_dir = os.path.abspath(args.out_dir) if args.out_dir else root

    try:
        registry = load_registry(registry_path)
        check_shape(registry)
        values = measure_all(registry, root)
        check_renderings(registry, values)
        pages = build_pages(registry, values, root, out_dir)
    except BuildError as e:
        print("%s: nothing written — %s" % (CHECK, e))
        return 1
    if not pages:
        print("%s: no page under %s carries a generated block" % (CHECK, out_dir))
        return 0
    for path in write(pages, out_dir):
        print("%s: wrote %s" % (CHECK, path))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

350	        "counts read: %s; commands run: `%s`; %s; the run took %.1f seconds against the %s seconds "
351	        "this registry expects; %s"
352	        % (", ".join(sorted(registry["counts"])), "`, `".join(commands), precondition_reach, elapsed,
353	           registry.get("expected_seconds", "unstated"), WHAT_IT_LEAVES_TO_A_PERSON)))
354	    return 0
355	
356

358	    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))
